summary.headline: Ester Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA up 103% to INR58.9 crore, margin 13.3% vs 8.3%, PAT INR18.6 crore vs loss INR7.2 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated performance improved sharply on higher film realisations, better utilisation (84%) and a richer VAS mix, with film EBIT rising to INR39.1 crore from INR6.9 crore. Ester Filmtech (100% subsidiary) turned EBITDA-positive at INR19.5 crore and PAT-positive at INR4.7 crore. Specialty Polymers volumes and revenue fell year on year on demand pressure in one high-margin product, though EBIT margin rose to 45.3%. Management said part of the other income (~INR10 crore) was one-time, and declined to give firm FY27/FY28 guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR7.2 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Ester Filmtech total income / EBITDA / PAT
financial_highlights.value: INR159.6 crore / INR19.5 crore (12.2% margin) / INR4.7 crore
financial_highlights.change: Income +62.7% YoY; PAT vs loss of INR16.5 crore

segments.name: Polyester Film (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Volumes 22,120 MT (+2.7% YoY); VAS volumes 6,368 MT (+23%), share of volume ~29% vs 24% a year ago. Capacity utilisation 84% vs 82%; BOPET standalone 85%.

segments.name: Specialty Polymers
segments.commentary: Volume 725 MT vs 954 MT; revenue INR32.7 crore vs INR48.1 crore. EBIT INR14.8 crore, margin 45.3% vs 31.7% on better product mix.

segments.name: rPET
segments.commentary: Volumes 1,394 MT (+19% YoY) and revenue INR17.5 crore (+24% YoY). Sequential volume decline attributed to captive use in packaging films; external sales expected to pick up from September.

segments.name: Ester Filmtech (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Sales volume 9,807 MT (+22.7% YoY); utilisation ~83%, highest so far. EBITDA INR19.5 crore vs loss of INR2.7 crore a year ago.

segments.name: Polyester chips
segments.commentary: Revenue around INR5 crore, driven by higher third-party sales volume.

segments.name: ELITe (50:50 JV with Loop Industries, not consolidated)
segments.commentary: Textile-to-textile chemical recycling plant in Gujarat, targeted for CY2028 commissioning; LOI for up to 15,000 MT/yr of fibre-grade resin from a global sports brand.

guidance_outlook: No firm FY27 or FY28 revenue, EBITDA or PAT guidance; management cited 'sustainable growth' in revenue and profitability.
Management expects good earnings for the next 6 to 8 quarters, supported by supply-demand balance and stable prices.
Management aims for VAS share of 50-60% over the next 2 to 3 years; about 35% by exit quarter of FY27.

Specialty Polymers: flat to single-digit growth in FY27, 20%+ revenue CAGR targeted over 3 to 5 years from FY28; absolute EBITDA and EBIT growth expected from FY28 even as percentage margins normalise.
Targeted FY27 gross debt repayment of about INR100 crore (gross debt to ~INR620 crore by year-end).
Management expects rPET to exceed 100% of rated capacity by exit of FY27; Q2 utilisation expected above Q1.
Management sees revenue reaching INR2,000-2,200 crore in 2 to 3 years from existing facilities (confirmed in answer to a question).
capex_capacity: Rated rPET capacity about 28,000 tons per annum (management also cited 30,000 TPA in prepared remarks).
No major capex planned for FY27 beyond sustenance and maintenance capex in standalone and Specialty Polymers.

ELITe: FEED completed by Tata Consulting Engineers; Toyo Engineering India appointed for detailed engineering; land acquisition expected to conclude within about 2 months; operations targeted CY2028. Debt for ELITe to be raised at JV level, not on Ester's balance sheet.
Industry BOPET capacity about 1.35 million tonnes; operating rate around 85%. Two lines added in the last 1.5 years; 2 to 3 more expected in the next 1.5 to 2 years.
Ester Filmtech utilisation about 83%, highest achieved so far.
demand_pricing: Spreads (value-add over raw material) for 12-micron corona commodity film were INR28-30 per kg in Q1; management said spreads are holding in the current quarter.
Value-added products carry a premium of INR25 or more over commodity; offline coated products command a higher premium still.
US tariffs moderated after the US Supreme Court rejected reciprocal tariffs; India regained lost US market share versus Q2-Q4 FY26.
Management said demand growth in India is well above capacity addition; early signs of similar BOPET demand shift in Europe.
PTA and MEG sourced locally under annual contracts (January-December); no production lost to raw material availability in Q1.
Specialty Polymers: demand pressure on one high-margin specialty product; pipeline expected to mature in H2, especially Q4.
